note: Re-judged 2026-11-14 by an independent auditor who authored neither 4aa1f84ff6 nor its test change. RFC 4724 Section 4 read: "The End-of-RIB marker MUST be sent by a BGP speaker to its peer once it completes the initial routing update (including the case when there is no update to send) for an address family after the BGP session is established." Stale unit TestInitialSyncMarkerWaitsForNoProcess re-read as committed: it names two route-pushing processes (sendUpdateOnly, sendRawOnly) plus an event-only listener, seeds the expectation set with the two pushers, and now raises the replay fence over both (raiseTestReplayFence sets replayFence and initialUpdateOwed), then runs the production sync body (runInitialSyncNow, Peer.sendInitialRoutes) with neither pusher reporting. It requires the sync to return within 2s, then asserts the fence is still up, zero reports credited (len apiSyncSignalled), and exactly the IPv4 unicast End-of-RIB bytes on the wire (eorWire equality). The deleted assertion (apiSyncReady channel still open) is replaced by fence-still-up plus no-credit over the same two silent processes: a sync that waited again for those reports, or for the fence to lower, never returns and goes red on the Eventually, and a marker missing or duplicated goes red on the byte equality. peer_initial_sync.go never reads initialUpdateOwed, so the extra assertions isolate that the marker left with the fence still raised. Question 1: the test asserts the RFC's own trigger, completion of ze's own initial update, not a process report. Question 2: yes, for a reintroduced wait or a missing marker. Question 3: the input is isolated, one negotiated family, no routes. Question 4: this unit proves the timing clause; the no-update case and every-family clause rest on the sibling positives below, unchanged. The tag's claim paragraph is unchanged and states no more than the body checks. The other cited units are byte-identical (TestInitialSyncEORReachesTheSilentFamilyToo only shifted). Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. Re-judged 2026-11-14 by an independent auditor who authored neither 08fe903803 nor the uncommitted phase 2 of spec-single-owner-lifecycle-2-bgp-session. Units read: TestInitialSyncEORReachesTheSilentFamilyToo, TestInitialSyncEORSentWhenNeitherSideDeclaredAFamily, TestInitialSyncMarkerWaitsForNoProcess, TestInitialSyncShutsTheQueueGateAndFreesTheRailsWithTheMarker, TestRFC4724EndOfRIBNotSentBeforeTheInitialUpdateCompletes (sync call only), and TestPredecessorSyncWritesNothingOnSuccessor (positive: the successor session carries exactly one UPDATE with the queued route, then the exact IPv4 unicast End-of-RIB, then no UPDATE for syncJoinProbe). checkNoFamilyEndOfRIB requires FRR's own bgp_update_receive_eor decode on the original session after the route arrived. Positives: sendInitialRoutes puts one End-of-RIB per negotiated family on the wire, including a silent family and a no-MP session. Negative TestRFC4724EndOfRIBNotSentBeforeTheInitialUpdateCompletes: while a plugin producing the initial update has not acknowledged peer-up, sendInitialRoutes is observed waiting and nothing is on the wire (EORSent 0); after the acknowledgement exactly the IPv4 unicast marker is written. Red on a marker sent ahead of the initial update or not sent after it. TestIsEndOfRIBAnyFamily is a neighbouring detector rule.
